By comparing the timestamps of the same MAC address from different roadside sensors, we can derive the travel time between the locations where the roadside sensors are located. 2.3.3 Traffic Control Traffic signals are arguably the most noticeable control mechanism in transportation. In addition, there are various other control mechanisms. • Traffic signal controllerscontrol the traffic lights at an intersection. Traditionally, the signal timing is de- termined by a time-of-day schedule which is periodically updated based on observed traffic counts. A signal controller with access to loop detectors can extend the duration of green periods given the existence of vehi- cles. With the advent of camera-based sensing and other real-time data sources, it is possible to use real-time traffic information at a larger scale to optimize traffic conditions (Wang et al. 2022). 11 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications • Traffic cabinetshouse the traffic signal controllers and other processing units and devices, connect to sensors and traffic lights, distribute electrical power to them, and provide an internet connection for remote monitoring and configuration. • Ramp meteringlimits vehicle flow from a ramp onto highways. Like signal control, it can be based on a fixed schedule, or be more responsive to traffic conditions. • Variable speed limitsare electronic speed limit signs which can change the displayed speed. These changes could be based on a schedule, automatically update based on real-time traffic or environmental conditions (light/dark, heavy rain, snow, fog, etc.), or via manual input from humans. Due to their variability, they provide much more flexibility than traditional signs. However, they are much more expensive, and their dependency on power to function may limit where they can be implemented. • Dynamic messaging signsprovide a method for transportation authorities to convey important information to drivers, such as weather warnings, travel times, or road closures. They can be used to direct traffic to an alternate route. 2.3.4 Vehicles and Fleets In vehicles, sensing and logging of vehicle data can occur. While this is of particular importance to fleets such as freight or public transit, it can also be used for personal vehicle sensing and diagnostics. When personal vehicle locations are tracked, special care has to be taken to protect the driver’s privacy, such as home address. • Fleet telemetricstrack the operational status (driving, stopped, ignition status, etc.), driving statistics (speed, fuel use, etc.), and work hours for each vehicle and driver. They are used to ensure compliance with safety regulations and have largely replaced manual record-keeping by drivers on paper. Furthermore, they can also be used to analyze vehicle efficiency and how it relates to routing, time of day, and other factors. • Vehicle loggingcan log similar information to telemetrics at an individual vehicle level. The information from connect Electronic Control Units (ECU) flowing in the Controller Area Network (CAN) bus can be access through On-Board Diagnostics II (OBD-II).
